headline: Investors fear AI will let customers shop around for better deals, cutting the profits of firms that rely on customer inertia.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1 because only the first lines of the article could be read.
importance_line: Customers could gain from easier price shopping, and companies that rely on customer inertia may lose profit, but this is the newspaper's reading of investor worries, not a measured effect.
summary: The Australian Financial Review reports that, after the sharp sell-off in software shares that traders nicknamed the "SaaSpocalypse", investors have a new concern: that AI tools will make it easy for consumers to compare and switch providers of services from holidays to banking, eroding profits that depend on customers not bothering to shop around.
notes: AFR paywalled after two sentences. Only the standfirst-level introduction was read, so key_facts are empty and the entry is treated as headline only.
